stem: A company runs SQL Server on an Azure virtual machine that its own team set up. It plans to move the database to Azure SQL Database, a managed database service. Under the shared responsibility model, which task moves from the company to Microsoft?

choices.text: Securing the physical servers, power and cooling in the datacenter that hosts the database's hardware.
Installing patches and updates for the database engine and the operating system that the database runs on.
Deciding which employees and applications are allowed to sign in to the database and read its tables.
Making sure the customer records loaded into the database are accurate, classified and kept only as long as needed.

stem: A manager asks which security duties stay with her company no matter whether it uses IaaS, PaaS or SaaS services in Azure. Which TWO responsibilities always remain with the customer? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The accounts and identities of the people, services and devices in the company's environment.
The power supply, cooling and building access controls of the datacenters that hold the hardware.
The physical hosts and the physical network inside the Azure datacenters that run the services.
The information and data that the company stores in its cloud services and applications.
The operating systems of the servers that run each service, including their security updates.

stem: A retailer runs a private cloud in its own datacenter, and company policy says customer payment records must stay there. Each holiday season its web storefront needs far more servers than the datacenter has for a few weeks. Which cloud model fits best?

choices.text: A private cloud only, buying enough additional servers for the holiday peak and keeping them in the datacenter all year.
A public cloud only, moving the storefront and the payment records to Azure so the datacenter can be closed down.
A hybrid cloud, keeping payment records in the private cloud and adding public cloud capacity for the holiday storefront.
A multicloud setup, running the storefront on two different public cloud providers at the same time for every season.

stem: A hospital group wants cloud-style self-service for its IT resources, but no other organization may share the hardware. It plans to rent a dedicated datacenter that a hosting company operates only for the group. Which cloud model is this?

choices.text: Private cloud, because the cloud resources are used by a single organization even though a third party hosts them.
Multicloud, because the resources involve two separate companies: the hospital group and the hosting provider.
Public cloud, because the datacenter is built and maintained by a third-party company rather than by the group's own staff.
Hybrid cloud, because the hardware belongs to one company while the resources are used by a different organization.

stem: A finance director asks how moving the company's servers from its own datacenter to Azure will change the way IT spending is recorded and planned. Which statement describes the consumption-based model correctly?

choices.text: Spending becomes a fixed annual fee that Microsoft sets in advance, whatever the company actually runs during that year.
Spending becomes capital expenditure, because the company buys an Azure subscription that is depreciated over several years.
Spending stays capital expenditure, because the company must still reserve its peak capacity before resources run.
Spending becomes operational expenditure, paid for the resources used, with no up-front purchase of server hardware.

stem: A company runs a line-of-business application on one VM size in one Azure region, 24 hours a day. It expects the same size and region for the next three years and the VM must not be interrupted. Which pricing option gives the deepest discount for this usage?

choices.text: Pay-as-you-go pricing, which bills each hour the VM runs at the standard rate with no commitment and no up-front payment.
An Azure savings plan, which commits to a fixed hourly spend that applies flexibly across eligible services and regions.
Azure Reservations, which commit to a specific resource, size and region for one or three years in return for a lower price.
Azure Spot Virtual Machines, which run on unused Azure capacity at a lower price and can be evicted whenever Azure needs it back.

stem: A small insurer needs to resize each photo that customers upload with a claim. Uploads arrive at random, from none for hours to hundreds in a few minutes. The team wants to write only the resize code and not pay for idle servers. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: Azure Virtual Desktop, which gives each claims handler a cloud desktop where the photos can be resized by hand as needed.
Azure Functions, which runs the resize code when an upload event arrives and charges only for the compute time it uses.
Azure Virtual Machines in a scale set that always keeps at least two instances running and adds more when CPU usage is high.
An Azure App Service plan that hosts the resize code as a web app with a fixed number of instances running around the clock.

stem: An online ticketing site must stay usable even when a server or other component fails during a major concert sale. Which cloud benefit does this requirement describe, and how does Azure state what customers can expect from each service?

choices.text: High availability, because the site must remain available despite disruptions, and Azure states uptime guarantees per service in SLAs.
Scalability, because Azure adds resources during the sale, and each service's expected uptime is printed in its Azure Pricing Calculator estimate.
Manageability, because the site is managed through the portal and APIs, and expected uptime is shown in each subscription's usage reports.
Governance, because policies keep the site compliant during the sale, and Azure states expected uptime in each region's compliance documents.

stem: A school's enrollment portal runs on two Azure virtual machines. On enrollment day traffic jumps tenfold, and the team adds eight more identical VMs, then removes them the next week. What type of scaling is this, and what is the main cost effect?

choices.text: Vertical scaling, because the portal's capacity goes up, and the school pays a one-time charge for the extra peak capacity used.
Vertical scaling, because adding identical VMs raises the CPU and memory of the existing two, and costs stay fixed afterwards.
Horizontal scaling, because it changes the size of each existing VM, and costs stay higher until the reserved capacity expires.
Horizontal scaling, because it adds and removes resource instances, and the school pays for the extra VMs only while they run.

stem: An architect explains that their order system is spread across several Azure regions, so that if one region suffers a disaster, the system recovers and keeps working from the others. Which cloud benefit is she describing?

choices.text: Predictability, which is the ability to forecast how much the system will cost and how it will perform in the coming months.
Governance, which is the ability to make sure that every deployed resource meets the company's technical and legal standards.
Reliability, which is the ability of a system to recover from failures and continue to function as users need it to.
Manageability, which is the ability to control the system through the portal, the CLI, APIs and PowerShell from anywhere.

stem: A retail company wants its online store to give customers consistently fast responses during unpredictable traffic, as part of the cloud benefit called performance predictability. Which TWO cloud capabilities support performance predictability? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The Azure Pricing Calculator, which estimates the monthly cost of the resources before they are deployed.
Load balancing, which spreads incoming traffic so that no single resource is overloaded by requests.
Resource tags, which label each resource with a cost center so that cloud spend can be split by team.
Usage tracking, which records resource consumption in real time so that future spend can be forecast.
Autoscaling, which adds resources when demand rises and removes them again when the demand drops.

stem: A bank must prove that every resource it deploys in Azure meets its technical standards and regulatory rules, and it wants to find any resource that drifts out of compliance. Which cloud capabilities describe the security and governance benefit it relies on?

choices.text: A multicloud setup that copies each resource to a second provider, plus cloud bursting that adds capacity on demand.
Templates that deploy resources to a defined standard, plus cloud-based auditing that flags resources out of compliance.
Vertical scaling that gives each resource more CPU and memory, plus horizontal scaling that adds instances during peak periods.
Spot pricing that runs resources on unused capacity, plus reservations that lock in a lower rate for compliant resources.

stem: Microsoft describes two kinds of manageability in the cloud: management of the cloud and management in the cloud. Which example belongs to management in the cloud?

choices.text: A new test environment is created from a preconfigured template, so that nobody has to configure its resources by hand.
A web app automatically adds more instances when its demand grows and then removes them again once the demand drops off.
A monitoring rule detects a failing resource in the environment and automatically replaces it with a new, healthy copy.
An administrator handles the company's Azure resources through the web portal, the command line, APIs and PowerShell.

stem: A manufacturer must move an old inventory application to Azure within a month. The application needs a specific operating system version and custom software installed on the server, and there is no time to redesign it. Which service type and Azure service fit best?

choices.text: IaaS, with Azure Virtual Machines where the company installs and controls the operating system and the software.
PaaS, with Azure App Service hosting the application on a platform whose operating system Microsoft manages.
PaaS, with Azure Functions running the application's code each time an inventory event arrives from the factory.
SaaS, buying a ready-made inventory application that the vendor runs and updates for all of its many customers.

stem: A three-person development team builds a web API in Python. They want to deploy code straight from their Git repository and get automatic scaling and high availability, without patching or licensing any operating system. Which option fits best?

choices.text: Azure Virtual Machines, where the team installs Python and a web server and then applies OS updates on its own schedule.
Microsoft 365, where the team publishes the web API inside the company's existing productivity apps for all of its users.
Azure App Service, a PaaS offering that hosts web apps and APIs while Microsoft maintains the platform beneath the code.
Azure Virtual Desktop, where each developer runs the API on a cloud desktop that can be reached from anywhere they work.

stem: A ten-person law firm has no IT staff. It needs email, calendars and document editing for every employee, and wants the provider to handle the servers, the application updates and their availability. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: SaaS, subscribing to a finished application such as Microsoft 365 that the firm simply signs in to and uses.
Private cloud, buying servers for a small on-site datacenter and installing mail and document software on them.
PaaS, writing its own mail and document application and hosting it on Azure App Service for the whole firm.
IaaS, running mail and document servers on Azure virtual machines that the firm configures and patches on its own.

stem: A company moves several servers to Azure virtual machines, an IaaS service. The IT team asks which duties it now has to carry out itself rather than Microsoft. Which TWO are the customer's responsibilities in IaaS? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Providing the physical security of the datacenter buildings and of the server racks inside them.
Keeping the datacenter's network connection to the internet available for all virtual machines.
Maintaining the physical hardware on which the virtual machines run inside the Azure datacenter.
Installing, configuring and patching the operating systems that run inside the virtual machines.
Configuring the virtual networks, subnets and network settings that the virtual machines will use.

stem: A consultant compares cloud service options for a client. Which option does Microsoft describe as the least flexible, but the easiest to get up and running and the one needing the least technical expertise?

choices.text: Infrastructure as a service (IaaS), because the provider hands over ready-made virtual machines with nothing else to set up.
Software as a service (SaaS), because the customer uses a fully developed application that the provider runs and maintains.
Serverless computing, because the provider runs event-driven code and the customer never sees or manages any servers.
Platform as a service (PaaS), because the provider maintains the operating system so that developers only deploy code.

stem: A company uses Microsoft 365 (SaaS). A former employee could still read shared files two weeks after leaving, because nobody disabled her account. The CIO asks whether this was Microsoft's failure under the shared responsibility model. What is the correct answer?

choices.text: Yes, because Microsoft runs the sign-in platform, so it is responsible for every account in the company's tenant and its use.
No, because user accounts are only a customer duty in IaaS, and this failure came from a datacenter problem on Microsoft's side.
No, because in SaaS the customer still manages its users and their access, while Microsoft runs the authentication platform.
Yes, because in SaaS the provider manages the whole stack, so Microsoft must remove accounts when employees leave a company.

stem: A company is planning four projects in Azure. For which project is platform as a service (PaaS) the most appropriate service type?

choices.text: Moving a legacy accounting server that depends on a custom kernel driver to Azure without changing any of its code.
Building a new customer portal on a managed platform that already includes built-in scaling and high availability.
Giving all staff a ready-made email and calendar service that they can start using right away with only a web browser.
Running a test lab where engineers install different operating system versions and reconfigure each one as needed.

stem: A small company plans to move a web app to Azure next quarter. Before anything is deployed, the owner wants a monthly cost estimate for an App Service plan, a managed database and storage, compared across two regions. Which tool should they use?

choices.text: Azure Advisor cost recommendations, which find underused resources in an existing subscription
A Cost Management budget, which sends an alert when actual spending passes a set threshold
Cost analysis in Microsoft Cost Management, which breaks down the charges of resources already running
The Azure pricing calculator, which models the planned services and options without deploying anything

stem: A team created a monthly budget in Microsoft Cost Management for its dev subscription with an alert at 100%. Spending passed the budget, the team received an email, but every VM kept running. What explains this?

choices.text: The budget failed because budgets apply only to resource groups and cannot be scoped to a whole subscription
The VMs kept running because a resource lock on the subscription overrides the budget's stop action
A budget only notifies when thresholds are reached; resources keep running unless an action group runs automation
Budgets stop resources only for production subscriptions, so the dev subscription was treated as exempt

stem: A company compares two deployment options and sees different monthly costs for what looks like the same workload. Which TWO factors can change the cost of Azure resources? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The region where the resources are deployed, because prices can differ between regions
Management groups placed above the subscriptions to organise policy and access
Tags attached to each resource for cost reporting and ownership tracking
How many resource groups the same resources are spread across in the subscription
Outbound data transfer leaving Azure datacenters, which is priced by billing zone

stem: Several departments share one resource group that holds a single application, and the resources cannot be split up. Finance wants monthly cost reports per department. What is the simplest approach?

choices.text: Create a management group for each department and move the shared resource group under all of them
Place a resource lock on each department's resources so their charges appear on a separate invoice
Assign an Azure Policy initiative per department so that compliance reports also show each team's spending
Apply a CostCenter tag to each resource and group the costs by that tag in Cost Management cost analysis

stem: An admin tagged a resource group with Environment=Prod. Later, cost analysis grouped by the Environment tag shows the VMs and disks inside that group as untagged. What is the reason?

choices.text: Resources do not inherit resource group tags, so tag each resource, for example by using Azure Policy
Tags take effect only on resources created by ARM templates, so resources made in the portal stay untagged
Tags on a resource group appear in cost analysis only after a resource lock is also applied to that group
Tag values are case-sensitive, so cost analysis ignores any tag whose name begins with an uppercase letter

stem: Admins of a production storage account must keep changing its settings, but nobody, including Owners, should be able to delete it by accident. Which control fits best?

choices.text: An Azure Policy assignment with the Allowed locations rule set to the storage account's current region
The Reader role for every admin on the storage account, so they can view it but not remove it
A Delete (CanNotDelete) resource lock on the storage account, which blocks deletion but allows changes
A ReadOnly resource lock on the storage account, which blocks deletion and keeps the settings editable

stem: A user with the Owner role tries to resize a VM and gets an error. The VM's resource group has a ReadOnly lock. What must happen before the resize can succeed?

choices.text: An Azure Policy remediation task must run, because locks are released when a policy marks resources compliant
The lock must be removed first, because locks apply to every user regardless of their role assignment
Microsoft support must approve the change, because only support can modify resources under a ReadOnly lock
The user must also be given the User Access Administrator role, which allows actions on locked resources

stem: A European company must make sure that no team can create Azure resources outside two approved EU regions, in every subscription. Which service should enforce this?

choices.text: Resource locks of type ReadOnly on each subscription, so that resources cannot be placed in other regions
Azure Policy, assigning the Allowed locations definition at a scope above the subscriptions
Microsoft Purview, scanning the subscriptions and classifying data stored outside the approved regions
Microsoft Defender for Cloud, which builds the approved region list from the subscription's secure score

stem: A retailer keeps data in Azure SQL Database, in on-premises SQL Server and in Amazon S3. Compliance staff need one map of where sensitive data is, with classification and lineage. Which service should they use?

choices.text: Microsoft Purview, for automated data discovery, classification and lineage across the whole estate
Azure Arc, which projects the S3 buckets and SQL servers into Azure and labels the sensitive columns
Azure Policy, which inspects the rows in each database and assigns a sensitivity label to each table
Azure Monitor Log Analytics, which collects data from all three sources into one workspace for queries

stem: A company assigns a new Azure Policy that allows only certain VM sizes. Some VMs created last year use a size not on the list. How does Azure Policy treat those existing VMs?

choices.text: It applies a ReadOnly lock to them, so that nobody can change them until they meet the new rule
It deletes them automatically, because Deny policies remove every resource that breaks the rule
It ignores them permanently, because a policy only ever applies to resources created after assignment
It evaluates them and reports them as noncompliant; they keep running unless the company remediates them

stem: An administrator works from a shared kiosk PC where installing software is blocked. They need to run a few Azure CLI commands against their subscription today. What should they use?

choices.text: An ARM template uploaded to a storage account, which runs the CLI commands when a file is added
Azure Arc, which connects the kiosk PC to Azure so commands can be run against the subscription
Azure Cloud Shell, a browser-based shell that is already authenticated and ships with the Azure CLI
Azure PowerShell installed locally on the kiosk PC, which provides the same commands as the Azure CLI

stem: A company runs Windows and Linux servers in its own datacenter and Kubernetes clusters in another public cloud. It wants to see them in Azure and apply the same Azure Policy rules it uses for Azure resources. Which service enables this?

choices.text: Azure Migrate, which discovers the on-premises servers and keeps managing them where they currently run
Azure ExpressRoute, which connects the datacenter to Azure so Azure Policy can reach the servers
Azure Arc, which projects servers and Kubernetes clusters outside Azure into Azure Resource Manager
Azure Site Recovery, which replicates the servers to Azure so they can be governed as Azure resources

stem: A team notices that a VM created in the Azure portal, with the Azure CLI or with Azure PowerShell behaves the same and obeys the same permissions. Why is that?

choices.text: Every request is approved by Azure Advisor, which checks it against best practices before deployment
Every request is first stored in Azure Monitor, which replays it to the resource in the same order
Every request runs inside Azure Cloud Shell, which converts portal clicks into the same Azure CLI commands
Every request from these tools goes to Azure Resource Manager, which authenticates and authorizes it

stem: A team must build identical dev, test and production environments many times a year. They want to describe the desired end state in files kept in source control and let Azure handle deployment order. What should they use?

choices.text: Bicep files deployed through Azure Resource Manager as declarative infrastructure as code
Step-by-step portal instructions in a wiki that each engineer follows for every new environment
Resource locks set on the dev environment and copied to test and production by Azure Policy
Azure Advisor recommendations exported to source control and replayed for each new environment

stem: A company moves from scripted, step-by-step deployments to ARM templates. Which TWO benefits of ARM templates should it expect? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Enforcement: after deployment the template blocks every manual portal change to the deployed resources
Declarative syntax: the template states which resources should exist instead of listing commands to run
Isolation: each template can contain only one resource, which keeps every deployment small and simple
Scope: a template can deploy only to the region of the subscription that the deploying user signed in from
Orchestration: Azure Resource Manager works out dependency order and deploys resources in parallel where it can

stem: A startup wants personalized suggestions to reduce spending on underused VMs and to improve the reliability and security of its existing Azure resources. Which service should it check?

choices.text: Azure Advisor, which evaluates existing resources and recommends changes for cost, reliability and more
Azure Service Health, which reports outages and planned maintenance for the Azure services and regions in use
The Azure pricing calculator, which estimates the cost of resources and options before they are deployed
Microsoft Purview, which scans the subscriptions and recommends cheaper storage tiers for classified data

stem: An operations team wants to be alerted automatically about outages and planned maintenance that affect the specific Azure services and regions it uses, not every Azure event worldwide. Which should it set up?

choices.text: A Cost Management budget alert, which emails the team when costs grow because of an Azure outage
Service Health alerts, based on a personalized view of the Azure services and regions the team uses
The Azure status page, which shows the health of all Azure services in all regions for every customer
Azure Advisor notifications, which report new recommendations to improve the configuration of resources

stem: Developers of a web app running partly in Azure and partly on-premises want to see request rates, response times, failure rates and slow dependency calls, and to test from outside that the site responds. What should they use?

choices.text: Azure Resource Health, which reports per-request response times and failures for each web server
Microsoft Cost Management cost analysis, which traces slow requests through their resource charges
Application Insights, which monitors web app performance and usage and supports availability tests
Azure Advisor performance recommendations, which measure response times for every request served

stem: Azure Monitor already collects logs from 40 VMs. An engineer needs to find every error event logged across all of them in the last hour and chart the trend over the past week. Which tool should they use?

choices.text: The Azure status page, which shows the errors from all VMs in a subscription for the selected period
Azure Resource Health, which lists the error events written by the operating system of each VM
Azure Advisor, which groups the error events of all VMs into recommendations sorted by severity
Log Analytics in the Azure portal, which runs queries against the log data that Azure Monitor collects

stem: An admin wants an SMS sent to the on-call engineer whenever a VM's CPU stays above 80% for 10 minutes. Which TWO Azure Monitor components are needed? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A Delete resource lock on the VM, so that Azure Monitor can read its CPU metrics continuously
An alert rule with a metric condition on the VM's CPU percentage over the 10-minute period
A Service Health alert that fires when Azure reports maintenance on the VM's host in the region
A Cost Management budget with a threshold based on the VM's forecasted compute spending
An action group that defines who is notified, such as the on-call engineer's phone number

stem: A company has twelve Azure subscriptions, one per department. The internal audit group must get read-only access to all of them, including subscriptions that are created later for new departments, without anyone repeating the setup for each subscription. What should the team do?

choices.text: Place the subscriptions under one management group and assign the Reader role to the audit group once at that scope
Assign the Reader role to the audit group on each subscription and repeat the assignment whenever one is created
Merge the departments into a single subscription and use resource tags to tell each department's resources apart
Move every department's resources into one shared resource group and assign the Reader role on that resource group

stem: A new Azure administrator is organizing a project's resources into resource groups. Which TWO statements about Azure resource groups are true? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A resource group can be nested inside another resource group to build a hierarchy of teams and their projects
One resource group can hold resources from several subscriptions, as long as those resources share one region
Deleting a resource group also deletes every resource that the resource group contains, so group by shared lifecycle
Every resource in a resource group must be deployed in the same Azure region as the resource group itself
Each resource belongs to exactly one resource group at a time, although many resource types can be moved to a different group

stem: A retailer runs its web tier on two VMs that sit in the same datacenter in the West Europe region. The app must keep running if a whole datacenter in that region loses power, and all data must stay inside West Europe. What should the team do?

choices.text: Put both VMs into an availability set so that Azure spreads them across separate fault and update domains
Switch the VMs' managed disks to zone-redundant storage while keeping both VMs in the current datacenter
Move one of the VMs to the paired region of West Europe so that the two copies sit in different regions
Deploy the VMs across two or more availability zones in West Europe and put a load balancer in front of them

stem: A software contractor is building a solution for a U.S. federal agency. The agency requires Azure datacenters that are physically and logically network-isolated from the main Azure cloud, operated by screened U.S. personnel, and backed by additional compliance certifications. Which option meets this requirement?

choices.text: Azure regions in China such as China North, which are operated through a partnership between Microsoft and 21Vianet
The East US region with its region pair, so that the agency's data is copied between two U.S. regions automatically
Azure Government regions such as US Gov Virginia and US Gov Arizona, which form a separate sovereign instance of Azure
Availability zones in the Central US region, combined with an Azure Policy that restricts deployments to that region

stem: During a design review, an engineer says: "We only deploy our VMs in East US. Because East US is paired with West US, Azure will fail our VMs over to West US automatically if East US has an outage." Which statement about region pairs is accurate?

choices.text: Pairing replicates every resource deployed in East US to West US and restarts the VMs there once an outage is detected
Paired regions are the only way to survive failures in Azure, so nonpaired regions cannot protect workloads against outages
Every Azure region has exactly one paired region in the same geography, so any region choice brings an automatic secondary
Pairing gives benefits such as staggered planned updates and prioritized recovery, but the team must design its own failover

stem: A team is splitting its existing website into a front end, a back end and a reporting service, so each part can be updated and scaled on its own. It wants to package each part with its dependencies as a lightweight unit that starts quickly, run several of them on one host, and not manage an operating system for each one, without rewriting the code. Which compute type fits best?

choices.text: Virtual machines, one for each part of the website, each running its own operating system that the team connects to and manages
Containers, one for each part of the website, run on a service such as Azure Container Apps that removes the container management overhead
Azure Functions, with each part of the website rewritten as small pieces of code that run only when an event such as an HTTP request triggers them
A virtual machine scale set that runs all three parts of the website together on every identical instance and adds instances when the load grows

stem: An online tax-filing service runs a custom application on Windows virtual machines because it needs specific operating-system settings. Traffic jumps sharply every evening and during the last days before the filing deadline. The company wants identical VMs added automatically during these peaks, removed afterward, and traffic spread across them. Which Azure service should it use?

choices.text: Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets with autoscale rules, placed behind a load balancer that spreads the traffic
An availability set that places the VMs across separate fault domains and update domains inside the datacenter
Azure Virtual Desktop host pools that give each customer a session on a shared Windows virtual machine
Azure Container Instances that start one container per customer whenever that customer begins a tax return

stem: A call center hires seasonal agents who work from their own personal laptops. Management wants every agent to use a full Windows desktop with the company's apps, with app data kept in Azure rather than on personal devices, and wants IT to manage these desktops centrally. Which Azure service should the company use?

choices.text: Azure App Service, which hosts the company's applications as web apps that agents open in their browsers
A separate Azure VM for each agent, each one given a public IP address so that the agent connects over RDP
Azure Virtual Desktop, which delivers centrally managed Windows desktops and apps from Azure to any device
Microsoft Entra Domain Services, which lets the agents' personal laptops join a managed domain in Azure

stem: A company has one virtual network in East US and another in North Europe, plus a small office whose only connection is an internet link. VMs in the two virtual networks must talk to each other privately over the Microsoft backbone, and the office needs an encrypted connection to the East US network over its existing internet link. Which TWO services should the company use? (Select TWO)

choices.text: An Azure ExpressRoute circuit from the office to the East US virtual network
An Azure DNS private zone shared by both virtual networks and the office
A private endpoint in each virtual network that points to the other network
Virtual network peering between the East US and North Europe virtual networks
A site-to-site connection through Azure VPN Gateway from the office to East US

stem: An application running on VMs in an Azure virtual network reads files from an Azure Storage account. The security team requires the VMs to reach the storage account through a private IP address taken from the virtual network, so that public network access to the account can be turned off. What should the team configure?

choices.text: A private endpoint for the storage account in a subnet of the virtual network, with public network access disabled
Virtual network peering between the VMs' virtual network and the storage account so that traffic stays on the backbone
A network security group rule on the VMs' subnet that allows outbound traffic only to the storage account's public endpoint
An Azure DNS private zone that gives the storage account a custom name inside the virtual network for the VMs

stem: A law firm must keep scanned case files in Azure Blob Storage for seven years. After the first month the files are almost never read, and when one is needed, waiting several hours for it is acceptable. The firm wants the lowest possible storage cost for these files. Which access tier should it use?

choices.text: Cool tier, an online tier for infrequently accessed data that is stored for at least thirty days at a time
Archive tier, an offline tier for rarely accessed data that can wait hours to be rehydrated before reading
Hot tier, an online tier for data in active use that has the lowest access cost but the highest storage cost
Cold tier, an online tier for rarely accessed data that must still be readable immediately when requested

stem: A company stores order documents in an Azure Storage account in a region that has availability zones and a paired region. The application must keep reading and writing the data if one availability zone in the primary region fails, and the company also wants a copy in a second region in case the whole primary region is lost. Which redundancy option meets both requirements?

choices.text: Zone-redundant storage (ZRS), which copies the data synchronously across availability zones in the primary region
Locally redundant storage (LRS), which keeps three copies of the data inside a single datacenter in the primary region
Geo-redundant storage (GRS), which keeps LRS copies in the primary region and replicates them to a secondary region
Geo-zone-redundant storage (GZRS), which uses ZRS in the primary region and also replicates to a secondary region

stem: A company with several branch offices runs a Windows file server in each office. It wants to centralize all file shares in Azure Files while users in every branch keep fast, local access through their Windows Server, with frequently used files cached locally and rarely used files kept in the cloud. Which service should it use?

choices.text: AzCopy run on a nightly schedule from every branch server to copy each office's changed files into Azure Files
Azure Data Box, which ships a physical storage device to each branch office to transfer the shares into Azure
Azure File Sync, which installs an agent on each Windows Server and keeps it synchronized with Azure Files
Azure Migrate, which discovers each branch file server and migrates it to an Azure virtual machine in a region

stem: A research lab must move tens of terabytes of microscope images from its on-premises storage into Azure Blob Storage once. Its internet connection is slow, so an online upload would take many weeks, and the lab needs no ongoing synchronization afterward. Which Azure service is the best fit for this transfer?

choices.text: Azure Data Box, an appliance that Microsoft ships to the lab to fill locally and send back for upload into Azure
Azure Storage Explorer, a graphical app that uploads files from the lab's workstation to a blob container online
Azure Migrate, a hub that discovers and assesses on-premises servers and then migrates them to virtual machines
Azure File Sync, an agent that keeps an on-premises Windows Server synchronized with a file share in Azure Files

stem: A storage administrator needs to upload a local folder of files to a blob container from a workstation and, later, copy blobs from one storage account to another. Which TWO tools are designed for these tasks? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Azure Data Box, a physical device that is shipped to the site for offline transfer
Azure Storage Explorer, a desktop app with a graphical interface for blobs and files
Azure Migrate, a hub that discovers, assesses and migrates servers and databases
Azure File Sync, an agent that keeps Windows file servers in sync with Azure Files
AzCopy, a command-line utility that copies blobs or files to, from and between accounts

stem: A company uses Microsoft Entra ID for sign-in. It wants users to be prompted for multifactor authentication only when they sign in from outside the company's trusted office network, and to be blocked when signing in from countries where the company does not operate. What should it configure?

choices.text: Microsoft Defender for Cloud just-in-time VM access, so that sign-ins from outside the office are allowed only for a limited time
Security defaults, so that every user registers for multifactor authentication and is prompted according to the location rules set by the admin
Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policies that use the sign-in location to require multifactor authentication or block access
Azure role-based access control, with a role assignment that requires multifactor authentication when users are outside the office

stem: An external contractor must be able to start, stop and resize the virtual machines in a resource group named rg-web, but must have no access to resources in any other resource group of the company's subscription. Which approach follows the principle of least privilege?

choices.text: Assign an Azure Policy to rg-web that grants the contractor's account permission to manage the VMs in that group
Assign the Virtual Machine Contributor role to the contractor's account at the scope of the rg-web resource group
Assign the Owner role at the subscription scope and ask the contractor to work only with the VMs that are in rg-web
Make the contractor's account a Global Administrator in Microsoft Entra ID so that it can manage any Azure resource

stem: A company is moving a legacy line-of-business application from its datacenter to Azure virtual machines. The application needs domain-joined servers, Group Policy, and LDAP and Kerberos authentication, and the company does not want to deploy, patch or back up domain controllers in Azure. Which service should it use?

choices.text: Microsoft Entra Domain Services, a managed domain that provides domain join, LDAP and Kerberos without DCs to run
Microsoft Entra ID alone, since its modern sign-in protocols also provide domain join, LDAP and Kerberos to VMs
Microsoft Entra External ID, which lets partner and customer users sign in to the application with their own identities
Microsoft Entra Connect, which synchronizes users from on-premises Active Directory into Microsoft Entra ID

stem: A security team protects workloads in Azure, on-premises servers connected through Azure Arc, and resources in AWS. It wants one service that continuously assesses their security posture, shows a secure score with prioritized hardening recommendations, and raises alerts when threats are detected. Which service should it use?

choices.text: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, which evaluates sign-in signals and blocks or challenges risky attempts to sign in
Azure Monitor, which collects metrics and logs from resources and fires alerts when the thresholds that you set are crossed
Azure Policy, which evaluates resources against assigned rules and reports which of them are compliant or noncompliant
Microsoft Defender for Cloud, which assesses posture, gives a secure score and recommendations, and detects threats

stem: A company used to trust any laptop connected to its office network. Under its new security model, a laptop on the office network is still checked for user identity, device health and sign-in risk before each access to an app, exactly as a laptop on a public network would be. Which Zero Trust principle does this mainly illustrate?

choices.text: Assume breach, which segments access to limit the blast radius and uses analytics to detect threats quickly
Use least privilege access, which limits every user to just-in-time and just-enough access with risk-based policies
Verify explicitly, which authenticates and authorizes every request based on all of the available data points
Defense in depth, which protects the data with several layers so that a breach of one layer is stopped by the next

stem: A CTO tells the board that cloud platforms "naturally support a reliable and resilient infrastructure." Which explanation of this claim matches how Microsoft describes cloud reliability?

choices.text: The cloud's decentralized design lets resources run in regions around the world, so a disaster in one region leaves others running.
The cloud provider contractually guarantees that no service will ever go down, so the customer never needs to plan for failure.
The cloud's preconfigured templates deploy every resource the same way, so configuration mistakes can never take a system down.
The pay-as-you-go model lets the company stop paying for resources during an outage, so failures cost the business nothing.

stem: An accounting firm runs its reporting app on one Azure virtual machine. At month-end the reports run out of memory, and the app cannot be split across several machines. The extra capacity is not needed the rest of the month. What should the firm do?

choices.text: Put a load balancer in front of the virtual machine, so that the month-end report requests are spread more evenly across its memory.
Scale up vertically by giving the virtual machine more CPU and RAM for month-end, then scale it back down once the reports finish.
Reserve a larger virtual machine size for three years, so that the extra memory is always available and paid for at a lower rate.
Scale out horizontally by adding identical virtual machines for month-end and removing them again once the reports are finished.

stem: A finance director worries that cloud bills will be impossible to forecast because charges follow consumption. Which cloud capability most directly supports cost predictability for her company?

choices.text: Autoscaling, which adds resource instances automatically when demand rises and removes them again once the demand drops.
Running the workload in several regions so that a catastrophic event in one region does not stop the whole application.
Load balancing, which redirects incoming requests from heavily used resources to less stressed ones so none is overloaded.
Real-time tracking of resource use combined with analytics that reveal spending patterns and trends for future planning.

stem: A software company wants strong security in the cloud, but it does not want its small IT team to spend time on operating system patches and routine maintenance. Which cloud strategy matches Microsoft's guidance for this security preference?

choices.text: Infrastructure as a service with more virtual machines, because extra machines reduce how often each one needs patches.
Infrastructure as a service, because it hands over physical resources and the company patches the operating systems itself.
A private cloud in the company's own datacenter, because its team then controls every patch on every server it operates.
Platform as a service or software as a service, because in those models patches and maintenance are handled automatically.

stem: A small online shop hosts its website on two servers in a rented rack. Floods of traffic from thousands of compromised machines keep knocking the site offline, and its two-person IT team cannot build defenses at that scale. Which cloud benefit addresses this most directly?

choices.text: Cost predictability, because real-time tracking of resource use shows what each traffic flood costs, so the shop can forecast its spend.
High availability, because Azure SLAs guarantee each service's uptime, so attack traffic can never take a site hosted in Azure offline.
Security, because cloud providers are typically well suited to handle these large-scale attacks, which makes the shop's network more robust.
Management in the cloud, because the team can reach the website's resources through the portal, the CLI, APIs or PowerShell at any time.

stem: A compliance officer is preparing a slide on the security and governance benefits of moving to the cloud. Which TWO items belong on that slide according to Microsoft's description of these benefits? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Cloud-based auditing flags resources that are out of compliance with the baseline and also provides mitigation strategies.
Autoscaling deploys additional resources when demand suddenly grows and then scales them back once the demand has dropped.
Resources can be managed through a web portal, a command line interface, APIs or PowerShell, whichever the team prefers.
Resources deployed in regions around the world keep the application running when one region suffers a catastrophic event.
Depending on the operating model, software patches and updates may be applied automatically, helping governance and security.

stem: Microsoft splits manageability into management of the cloud and management in the cloud. An operations lead lists five features. Which TWO are examples of management of the cloud? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Administrators open the Azure portal in a web browser to review and change the settings of the company's resources.
The health of resources is monitored, and a resource that is failing is automatically replaced with a healthy one.
A deployment tool calls the Azure APIs directly from the company's release pipeline to create and update resources.
Engineers run PowerShell scripts from their laptops to automate recurring changes to the company's Azure resources.
Automatic alerts are sent based on configured metrics, so the team is aware of resource performance in real time.

stem: A QA team must quickly copy an approved server configuration into several test environments, start and shut them down as test cycles change, and keep complete control of each operating system. Which cloud service type fits best?

choices.text: Infrastructure as a service, using virtual machines that can be created from the approved configuration and switched on and off.
Serverless computing, running each test as a short function that the platform starts on demand and removes once it finishes.
Platform as a service, deploying the test builds to a managed hosting platform where Microsoft maintains the operating system.
Software as a service, subscribing to a ready-made test management application that the vendor runs and updates for the team.

stem: An engineering firm runs fluid dynamics simulations with its own solver software, which needs a specific Linux version, tuned libraries and many high-performance processors. Which Azure option fits best?

choices.text: Microsoft 365, which gives every engineer cloud versions of desktop applications that can run the simulations in the browser.
Azure virtual machines from the HPC-optimized H family, where the firm installs and tunes its own operating system and solver.
Azure SQL Database, which stores the simulation input data in a managed database engine that Microsoft keeps patched and updated.
Azure App Service, which hosts the solver as a web app on a managed platform whose operating system Microsoft maintains for the firm.

stem: A retail chain's analysts want to mine three years of sales data to find buying patterns and predict demand for next season. They do not want to install, license or patch any servers or analytics software. Which service type fits best?

choices.text: Software as a service, using the company's email and office suite to share sales spreadsheets among analysts in each store.
On-premises servers, buying an analytics appliance for the head office and running the analysis on the company's own hardware.
Infrastructure as a service, building a cluster of virtual machines and installing and patching the analytics software on each one.
Platform as a service, using analytics tools offered as a managed service so the provider maintains the servers and the software.

stem: A distributor's sales team has no developers. Instead of building its own customer relationship management (CRM) system, it plans to subscribe to Dynamics 365 Sales, a software as a service (SaaS) application. Which trade-off comes with this choice?

choices.text: It gets full control of the application's code and platform, but its own staff must patch the operating systems that run the CRM application.
It avoids buying any servers, but it must hire developers to keep the CRM's runtime, middleware and database engine patched and up to date.
It gets the fastest start with the least technical skill, but it is limited to the features and settings that the vendor's application offers.
It hands over all operational work, but ownership of the customer records it stores moves to Microsoft, along with responsibility for them.

stem: A new cloud architect is classifying the Azure and Microsoft services his company uses. Which TWO of these services are platform as a service (PaaS) offerings? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Azure Virtual Machines, which run the company's own operating system images on hardware in Azure datacenters.
Microsoft 365, which gives the company's employees email, calendars and office applications as finished services.
Azure SQL Database, which provides a managed database engine that Microsoft maintains, patches and keeps updated.
Azure Disk Storage, which provides the managed disks attached to the company's virtual machines for their data.
Azure App Service, which hosts the company's web apps and APIs without the team managing the servers below them.

stem: A team hosts its web app on Azure App Service (PaaS). During a review it asks which responsibility area is shared between the team and Microsoft in PaaS, rather than owned entirely by one side. Which area is it?

choices.text: Network controls, because Microsoft provides baseline network security while the team configures application-level network controls.
The physical hosts that run the app, because the team chooses the pricing tier and the number of instances that the hosts must provide.
The operating system of the servers that run the app, including its security updates, because the team picks the runtime version.
The customer data that the app stores, because Microsoft holds copies of it in its datacenters and is responsible for its classification.

stem: A company runs its own mail server software on an Azure virtual machine (IaaS) and moves every mailbox to Microsoft 365 (SaaS). In Microsoft's shared responsibility matrix, which TWO areas go from the customer's responsibility in IaaS to Microsoft's alone in SaaS? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The mail application, including how the company configures it and controls who can use its features and data.
The client devices that employees read their mail on, including their endpoint protection and their compliance.
The identities and user accounts of employees, including creating them and removing them when staff members leave.
The operating system of the servers that run the mail service, including installing all of its security updates.
Network controls such as the firewall rules and segmentation that protect the servers running the mail service.

stem: A trainer asks students to order the three cloud service types from the one that gives the customer the most control and responsibility to the one that gives the least. Which order is correct?

choices.text: SaaS first, then PaaS, then IaaS, because software services leave the most decisions to the customer.
IaaS first, then PaaS, then SaaS, because the provider takes over more of the stack at each later step.
PaaS first, then IaaS, then SaaS, because platform services expose the most settings to the customer.
IaaS first, then SaaS, then PaaS, because software services still need the customer to manage the runtime.

stem: A startup's developers move to platform as a service (PaaS) to get a complete development environment. Besides the physical infrastructure, physical security and internet connection, what does the cloud provider maintain for them?

choices.text: The startup's user accounts, roles and access policies, including deciding which developers may deploy code.
The application code that the developers write, including fixing security defects that are found in that code.
The business data that the application stores, including deciding how long each kind of record is retained.
The operating systems, middleware, development tools and analytics services that make up the cloud solution.

stem: A company moved its customer portal from its own servers to Azure App Service. A security test then finds that the portal's code is open to SQL injection. A manager says Microsoft must fix it because the app now runs on PaaS. Is the manager right?

choices.text: No, because in PaaS the customer stays responsible for its application code and security, while Microsoft runs the platform.
No, because App Service is an IaaS offering, so the customer patches the operating system and the code on its virtual machines.
Yes, because in PaaS Microsoft manages the runtime, so any flaw in an application running on it is Microsoft's to fix.
Yes, because in PaaS Microsoft takes over network controls entirely, and network filtering is how SQL injection is prevented.

stem: A team runs a standard .NET web app on five Azure virtual machines and spends many hours each month on operating system patches and server maintenance. The app needs no custom OS changes. Which move reduces this effort, and what is the trade-off?

choices.text: Stay on IaaS but add more virtual machines, giving up some budget so that each VM carries less load and needs fewer OS patches.
Move to PaaS with Azure App Service, giving up direct control of the operating system in exchange for Microsoft maintaining it.
Move to SaaS by rebuilding the app inside Microsoft 365, giving up the ability to choose which features the company's customers see.
Move to a private cloud in the company's own datacenter, giving up the pay-as-you-go pricing model while keeping full OS control.

stem: A company runs an application on Azure virtual machines (IaaS). After a change, the VMs can no longer reach an external partner service, because a network security rule that the company's own admins created blocks the traffic. Who must fix it?

choices.text: The partner, because outbound traffic from Azure VMs is managed by the destination service once it has left the Azure datacenter.
Microsoft, because in IaaS the provider is responsible for network connectivity to the internet, including every rule that controls it.
The company, because in IaaS the customer is responsible for network configuration, including the security rules it created.
Microsoft, because the physical network is always the provider's job, and every network rule in Azure runs on the physical network.

stem: A company's solution uses Azure Functions to run code when orders arrive, Azure virtual networks to connect its virtual machines, and Dynamics 365 for its customer service staff. Which classification matches Microsoft's shared responsibility guidance?

choices.text: Azure Functions is SaaS, the virtual networks are IaaS, and Dynamics 365 is PaaS.
Azure Functions is IaaS, the virtual networks are PaaS, and Dynamics 365 is SaaS.
Azure Functions is PaaS, the virtual networks are IaaS, and Dynamics 365 is SaaS.
Azure Functions is PaaS, the virtual networks are SaaS, and Dynamics 365 is IaaS.

stem: A security team wants to track about twenty related security rules as one compliance goal. It wants to assign them to each subscription as a single item and add more rules later without creating new assignments. What should it create?

choices.text: A policy exemption that bundles the twenty rules so they can be tracked together on one report
A policy initiative that groups the related policy definitions and is assigned as one unit
A management group that holds the twenty rules and applies them to each subscription below it
A custom Azure RBAC role that contains the twenty rules as permissions for the security team

stem: A company plans a rule that storage accounts must not allow public blob access. Before blocking anything, it wants to see which existing and new accounts break the rule while teams keep deploying normally. Which policy effect should it use first?

choices.text: Audit, which marks noncompliant resources and logs a warning but lets every request continue
DeployIfNotExists, which deploys a private endpoint for every account that allows public access
Deny, which rejects noncompliant requests and lists every blocked account on the dashboard
Modify, which changes the public access setting on each account as it is created or updated

stem: Finance requires a CostCenter tag on every resource. New resources missing the tag should get a default value automatically, and hundreds of existing untagged resources should be fixed as well. What should the company use?

choices.text: An Azure Policy with the Deny effect, which blocks untagged resources and retags existing ones in bulk
A Delete lock on each resource group, which requires every resource to carry the tag before changes
An Azure Policy with the Audit effect, which adds the missing tag during the daily compliance evaluation
An Azure Policy with the Modify effect that adds the tag, plus a remediation task for existing resources

choices.text: Assign the more permissive policy to the subscription as well, so the newer assignment overrides the older one
Place a ReadOnly lock on the resource group, which pauses policy evaluation for the resources inside it

choices.text: The Owner role cannot create storage accounts, because only the Storage Account Contributor role is able to
A resource lock on the subscription blocks every new storage account until the lock owner approves it
The subscription's spending budget was exceeded, so Azure blocks any new premium storage account request

A Delete lock on a VM also stops authorized users from changing its settings, such as its size

choices.text: Everything is deleted, because a lock on a single resource is ignored when its parent group is deleted
The entire delete operation is blocked, so none of the twelve resources or the group are deleted
The eleven unlocked resources are deleted, and the group remains with only the locked VM inside it

stem: An admin puts a ReadOnly lock on the logical server that hosts an Azure SQL database. The ordering application keeps inserting and updating rows without errors. Why does the lock not stop these writes?

choices.text: Locks apply only to control plane operations on the resource; data plane writes to the database are not restricted
A ReadOnly lock on a logical server covers only its firewall rules, while each database needs its own separate lock
ReadOnly locks take effect only after the next daily compliance evaluation cycle, so writes continue until it runs

stem: A governance team relies on the Azure Policy compliance dashboard. Which TWO events cause Azure Policy to evaluate resources and update their compliance state? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A VM in the scope runs at high CPU and Azure Monitor records the new metric values
A user with the Reader role opens the resource's overview page in the Azure portal
The subscription's monthly invoice is generated and the charges are posted in Cost Management
The standard compliance evaluation cycle, which reevaluates assignments once every 24 hours

stem: A new operations manager has no scripting experience. She wants to create a few resources with guided forms and build a personal dashboard that shows the health of her team's key resources. Which tool should she use?

choices.text: The Azure CLI, a command-line tool whose commands can be chained together in Bash scripts
Azure Arc, which projects resources into Azure Resource Manager so they appear in one inventory

Azure PowerShell, a set of cmdlets that return objects and can be combined into reusable scripts

choices.text: The Azure CLI, whose commands follow Bash-style syntax and feel most natural on Linux systems
Azure PowerShell, the Az module whose verb-noun cmdlets return objects in a PowerShell session
Azure Arc, which runs the existing on-premises PowerShell scripts against Azure resources
The Azure portal, whose graphical blades can be recorded as PowerShell scripts for later reuse

stem: A company is choosing between the Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell for its administrators. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The Azure CLI runs in Bash, Cmd or PowerShell, while Azure PowerShell needs a PowerShell session
The Azure CLI runs only inside Azure Cloud Shell and cannot be installed on a local workstation

stem: An administrator uses Azure Cloud Shell every day and keeps helper scripts and SSH keys in her home directory. She wants those files to still be there in tomorrow's session. What makes this possible?

choices.text: The browser's local storage, which keeps a copy of the Cloud Shell file system on her own computer
The Cloud Shell host VM, which Microsoft keeps running for each user between sessions indefinitely
An Azure Files share in a storage account that Cloud Shell mounts and uses to persist her $HOME directory

stem: An auditor has only the Reader role on a subscription. She opens Azure Cloud Shell from the portal and runs an Azure CLI command to stop a VM, but the command fails with an authorization error. Why?

choices.text: Cloud Shell needs Azure Arc enabled on the VM before any command can change the machine's state
Cloud Shell signs in as her own account, so commands are limited to the permissions her roles grant

stem: Every Monday an engineer performs the same fifteen portal steps to create a test resource group, a storage account and a VM. Mistakes are common, and colleagues need to repeat the task the same way. What is the best improvement?

choices.text: Connect the test machines to Azure Arc so the portal remembers and replays the previous week's steps
Place a Delete lock on the resource group so the engineer can reuse it instead of creating it each week

stem: A hospital must keep a patient database in its own datacenter, but wants it to run as Azure SQL Managed Instance on its local Kubernetes cluster, with Azure-style updates and a unified view in the Azure portal. Which option fits?

choices.text: Azure SQL Managed Instance in the nearest Azure region, reached from the hospital over ExpressRoute
SQL Server on an Azure virtual machine in a region close to the hospital, managed from the portal
Azure Migrate, which assesses the database and moves it into an Azure SQL service in a region
Azure Arc-enabled data services, which run SQL Managed Instance on Kubernetes outside Azure

stem: A company plans to connect forty physical Linux and Windows servers in its datacenter to Azure Arc. What must happen on each server for it to appear and be managed in Azure?

choices.text: Azure Stack hardware replaces the server, and the workload is reinstalled onto the new hardware
The Azure Connected Machine agent is installed, and the server then gets its own Azure resource ID
The server is migrated into an Azure virtual machine, and the original machine is switched off

stem: An admin plans to onboard the company's existing Azure VMs to Azure Arc so that Azure Policy and tags can be applied to them. A colleague says this is unnecessary. Why is the colleague right?

choices.text: Azure VMs are already Azure Resource Manager resources; Arc-enabled servers is designed for machines outside Azure
Azure VMs are governed by Azure Arc automatically, because every new VM is enrolled in Arc at creation time

stem: A software company runs Kubernetes clusters on premises and in another cloud, next to its AKS clusters. It wants to see every cluster in one Azure inventory and push configuration to all of them from a Git repository. What should it use?

choices.text: Azure Kubernetes Service, after rebuilding every on-premises and other-cloud cluster as a new AKS cluster

stem: In a briefing, an architect says Azure Arc "projects" on-premises servers into Azure Resource Manager. What does this mean for those servers?

choices.text: Each server is converted into an Azure virtual machine, and the on-premises copy becomes a read-only image
Each server appears as an Azure resource that can be organized, tagged and governed while it keeps running on-premises
Each server's disks are uploaded to Azure Storage so that its data is backed up and stored inside Azure

stem: A developer deleted a test VM last month. This month, cost analysis still shows charges in the same resource group for a managed disk and a public IP address. What is the most likely reason?

choices.text: Azure keeps billing a deleted VM's disk and IP address for a fixed retention period and then removes them automatically
The resource group itself carries a monthly charge that cost analysis splits across the disk and IP address meters
Deleting a VM can leave its disks, IP addresses and other network resources behind, and they keep billing until removed
Cost analysis shows the deleted VM's final compute charges under its disk and IP meters until the billing cycle closes

stem: A team deploys a VM from Azure Marketplace with a third-party firewall product preinstalled. The bill is higher than for the same VM size built from a plain Linux image. What explains the difference?

choices.text: Marketplace deployments add a Microsoft support plan to the subscription automatically and bill it with the VM
Marketplace images always run in a premium capacity tier that raises the compute rate for the selected VM size

stem: A student uses an Azure free account and runs a few small services for weeks without being charged. A colleague with a pay-as-you-go subscription is billed for similar usage. Which cost factor best explains the difference?

choices.text: Subscription type, because some subscriptions include usage allowances such as free products and starting credit

Geography, because free accounts are limited to regions where Microsoft does not charge for these services

stem: An architect reads that outbound data transfer prices depend on "zones" and assumes this means the availability zones inside a region. What is a billing zone in Azure?

choices.text: A geographical grouping of Azure regions used for data transfer pricing, which is different from an availability zone
A physically separate group of datacenters inside one region, each with its own power, cooling and networking
A pair of regions in the same geography that Microsoft uses to order platform updates and regional recovery
A logical container inside a subscription that groups resources so their costs show up on one invoice line

stem: A company uploads large archive files into Azure Blob Storage every month and almost never downloads them. The finance lead worries about bandwidth charges. Which statement about data transfer is accurate?

choices.text: Inbound and outbound transfers are billed at the same rate, so the monthly upload volume drives most of the bandwidth charge here
Data transfer is priced per availability zone, so keeping the archive in a single zone removes any bandwidth charge
