stem: A company on an Enterprise Agreement has divided its enrollment into departments, each with a spending quota. The head of HR wants an email when HR's spending reaches a set percentage of its quota. Which alert type in Cost Management covers this?

choices.text: A Service Health alert, which emails administrators when an Azure service issue affects a region HR uses
A department spending quota alert, which emails department owners when spending reaches a threshold of the quota
A credit alert, which emails account owners as the organisation's Azure Prepayment balance is consumed
An activity log alert, which emails administrators whenever someone creates or deletes resources in HR's subscriptions

stem: An administrator opens the cost alerts view in Microsoft Cost Management to review every type of alert it collects. Which TWO alert types appear there? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Metric alerts raised when a VM's CPU percentage stays above a set threshold
Activity log alerts raised when someone deletes a resource in the subscription
Credit alerts raised as an Enterprise Agreement's Azure Prepayment is consumed
Service Health alerts raised when an Azure outage affects a region you use
Budget alerts raised when spending reaches a threshold defined on a budget

stem: A project manager wants to be warned before the project's monthly spending actually passes its budget, based on where spending is trending. What should be configured in Microsoft Cost Management?

choices.text: A budget with a forecasted alert, which fires when projected cost is expected to exceed the set threshold
An Azure Advisor cost recommendation, which warns when month-to-date spending is trending above the budget
A credit alert, which warns at fixed percentages before the subscription's spending passes its budget amount
A budget with an actual-cost alert at 100%, which fires early whenever daily spending rises faster than usual

stem: After a new release, a company's Azure bill rose sharply compared with last month. The operations lead wants to see which services and regions caused the increase. Which tool should they use?

choices.text: Azure Service Health, which reports service incidents and planned maintenance that affect the regions you use
The Azure pricing calculator, which compares monthly estimates for the same services across regions and tiers
Cost analysis in Microsoft Cost Management, which breaks down actual costs by service, region, resource and time
Azure Monitor metrics explorer, which charts performance counters such as CPU and network throughput over time

stem: A company prices the same VM size, operating system and settings in two Azure regions and sees a different hourly rate in each. Nothing else about the configuration differs. What explains the price difference?

choices.text: Some regions include a paid Microsoft support plan in every VM's rate, which raises the hourly price in those regions
Prices are set by the distance between the region and the subscription's billing address, so far regions cost more
Regions with availability zones copy each VM into every zone automatically, so the rate covers several VM copies
Local costs such as power, labor, taxes and fees vary by location, so the same resource can cost more in one region

stem: Operations wants to mark which of the company's 2,000 Azure resources are mission-critical. An engineer says the Impact tag must then be added to every resource, including test resources. What is accurate?

choices.text: Tags can be set only while a resource is being created, so existing resources must be redeployed to receive the Impact tag
Tags are optional per resource, so Impact can go only on mission-critical resources and untagged ones count as not critical
Azure requires every resource in a subscription to carry the same tag names, so the Impact tag must be added everywhere
Azure gives resources tagged Impact=Mission-critical a higher service level, so tagging test resources would add cost

stem: Operations wants a nightly script to stop all development and test VMs. These VMs are spread over many resource groups and subscriptions, mixed in with production VMs. What is the simplest way for the script to target only the right VMs?

choices.text: Move the non-production VMs into one management group so the script can stop everything in that group
Move the non-production VMs into a separate Azure region so the script can stop every VM in that region
Create a budget for each resource group so that budget alerts stop the non-production VMs every night
Tag each VM with an Environment value such as Dev or Test and have the automation select VMs by that tag

stem: A cloud team is writing a tagging strategy and lists possible reasons for tagging resources. Which TWO are documented uses of resource tags in Azure? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Grouping resources by how critical their availability is to the company's operations
Encrypting the data stored in a resource with a key chosen by its classification tag
Lowering the hourly rate charged for resources tagged as part of a production workload
Blocking deletion of every resource that carries a specific tag value such as Prod
Classifying resources by the security level of their data, such as public or confidential

stem: A studio renders animation frames in nightly batch jobs. Each job saves its progress and simply restarts if its VM is stopped partway. The VMs are not needed during the day, and the studio wants the lowest compute cost. Which pricing option fits best?

choices.text: Reservations for the render VM size, which commit to that specific capacity for every hour of a one- or three-year term
Azure Spot Virtual Machines, which run on unused Azure capacity at a lower price but can be evicted when Azure needs it
Pay-as-you-go pricing with no commitment, which bills each hour the render VMs run at the standard on-demand rate
An Azure savings plan for compute, which commits to a fixed hourly spend on eligible compute for one or three years

stem: A manager built an estimate in the Azure pricing calculator that includes several VMs and premium storage. She worries that the subscription is now being charged and that the total is a fixed price. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: The calculator deploys trial copies of the selected resources, billed at a reduced rate until they are removed
The calculator reserves the selected resources for a short period and charges for them only if they are deployed
Nothing is provisioned or charged by the calculator, and its total is an estimate given for information only
The calculator total is a binding quote that Microsoft honours for the selected region and configuration

stem: A team creates two VMs of the same size, in the same region and subscription, running around the clock. One runs Windows Server and the other runs Linux, and their costs differ. Which cost factor explains this?

choices.text: Resource type and settings, because operating system licensing is part of what a VM's configuration costs
Subscription type, because each operating system is billed under its own subscription offer within Azure
Geography, because the operating system decides which datacenter in the region physically hosts each VM
Consumption, because Windows VMs are always metered for more hours than Linux VMs in the same billing cycle

stem: A law firm's compliance team must find data risks and manage regulatory compliance requirements for content stored in Microsoft Teams, OneDrive and Exchange, and protect sensitive data across clouds, apps and devices. Which service fits?

choices.text: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, which assesses the security posture of cloud workloads and recommends hardening steps
Microsoft Purview, a family of data governance, risk and compliance solutions that gives one view of the firm's data
Microsoft Entra ID Protection, which detects risky sign-ins and compromised accounts and can require extra checks
Azure Policy, which evaluates Azure resource settings against rules and reports which resources are noncompliant

stem: Business analysts at a manufacturer struggle to find trustworthy datasets spread across Azure databases, on-premises servers and another cloud. Data owners want one secure place where analysts can discover and understand data, with access managed at scale. Which service fits?

choices.text: Azure resource tags on each database and server, so that analysts can search the portal for resources owned by data teams
Azure Storage Explorer, a desktop tool that lets analysts browse and download data from the storage accounts they can reach
Microsoft Purview, whose Data Map and Unified Catalog govern data across on-premises, multicloud and SaaS sources
An Azure Monitor Log Analytics workspace, which collects logs from many sources so analysts can query them in one place

stem: Auditors ask a data team to show how the figures in a finance report flow from the source systems through each processing step to the final report. The data lives on-premises and in Azure. Which service provides this view?

choices.text: Application Insights in Azure Monitor, which traces each request as it flows through an application's components
Azure Network Watcher, which traces the path that network packets take between a source and a destination
The Azure activity log, which records each control-plane operation performed on the resources in a subscription
Microsoft Purview, which records end-to-end data lineage from data sources through processing to reports

stem: A new chief data officer reads that Microsoft Purview is made up of two main solution areas and asks which ones they are. Which TWO are the main solution areas of Microsoft Purview? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Resource governance, which enforces allowed regions and VM sizes in subscriptions
Cost governance, which tracks data service spending against each department's budget
Identity governance, which reviews who holds privileged roles in Microsoft Entra ID
Risk and compliance, which uses Microsoft 365 services to manage and monitor data
Unified data governance across on-premises, multicloud and SaaS data sources

stem: A company deployed staging and production a year ago. Since then, engineers fixed production issues by changing settings in the portal, and new releases now pass in staging but fail in production. Which practice prevents this kind of problem?

choices.text: Infrastructure as code: keep the environment definition in source control, change the file, and redeploy it to every environment
Resource locks: put a ReadOnly lock on the staging environment so that it can never drift away from the production settings
Activity log alerts: email the team whenever someone changes a production setting so that staging can be updated to match
Management groups: move both subscriptions under one management group so that their settings are always kept in sync

stem: A team deploys an ARM template that creates a storage account. A week later it deploys the same template again, unchanged, and the storage account still has exactly the properties the template defines. What happens?

choices.text: A second storage account is created with a generated suffix, because each deployment adds a new set of resources
Resource Manager deletes the storage account and creates a new, empty one, because each deployment starts over
Resource Manager sees the storage account already matches the template, so the resource is left in that same state
The deployment fails, because a template can create a resource only once and must be edited before it runs again

stem: An organization has one management group with several subscriptions. An admin wants a setting to apply to every resource group in the Sales subscription, including groups created later, without affecting the other subscriptions. At which Azure Resource Manager scope should it be applied?

choices.text: The management group, because settings applied there reach only the resource groups that already exist at that time
The Sales subscription, because settings applied there are inherited by all of its resource groups and their resources
Each existing resource group in Sales, because resource groups created later copy the settings of an existing group
Each resource in Sales, because Resource Manager applies settings only at the level of individual resources

stem: A team writes its Azure infrastructure in ARM template JSON and finds the files long and hard to read. It is considering Bicep. Which TWO statements about Bicep are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Bicep deployments go straight to each resource provider, so they skip the Azure RBAC checks done by Resource Manager
Bicep is an imperative scripting language that runs each command in order, unlike the declarative JSON templates
Bicep has no state file for the team to store, because Azure keeps track of the state of the deployed resources
Bicep supports only resource types that are generally available, so newer preview types still need a JSON template
A Bicep file is converted into an ARM JSON template during deployment, and Resource Manager deploys it as usual

stem: A team's single ARM template for its whole solution has grown to thousands of lines, and three other projects need the same virtual network setup. Which ARM template capability helps most?

choices.text: Deployment scripts: add a Bash or PowerShell script to the template that copies the network into every project's subscription
Modular files: split the template into smaller templates linked from a main template, and reuse the network one in each project
Resource tags: tag the network resources in the template so that every other project's deployment includes them automatically
Management groups: store the template at the management group so each subscription below it inherits the virtual network

stem: A developer deploys an ARM template that contains a syntax error. Resource Manager rejects the deployment before creating any resource, so nothing is left half-built. Which ARM template feature explains this?

choices.text: Azure Policy deny effect: a built-in policy blocks every template that contains an error before it is deployed
Azure Advisor checks: Advisor reviews each template against best practices and stops those with problems
Resource locks: a CanNotDelete lock on the resource group rolls back any template that contains an error
Built-in validation: Resource Manager checks the template first and starts the deployment only after it passes

stem: Azure Advisor shows a recommendation to create Azure Service Health alerts so the team learns about service issues and planned maintenance. In which Advisor category does this recommendation appear?

choices.text: Operational excellence, which covers process and workflow efficiency, resource manageability and deployment practices
Security, which covers threats and vulnerabilities that could lead to a breach of the resources in the subscription
Performance, which covers changes that improve the speed and responsiveness of the applications that are running
Reliability, which covers the continuity of business-critical applications and flags configuration risks for them

stem: A security lead notices that Azure Advisor lists security recommendations, such as enabling disk encryption or closing management ports. Where do these Advisor security recommendations come from?

choices.text: Microsoft Purview, whose data classification scans produce security tasks for every storage account in Advisor
Azure Policy, whose compliance results for every assigned initiative are copied into Advisor as security items
Microsoft Entra ID Protection, whose risky sign-in detections are listed in Advisor as resource security tasks
Microsoft Defender for Cloud, whose security assessments of the resources are shown in Advisor's security category

stem: A finance team wants an email whenever Azure Advisor produces a new cost recommendation for resources in one resource group, instead of checking the Advisor dashboard by hand. What should be set up?

choices.text: A Cost Management budget on that resource group, which emails when Advisor publishes a new recommendation
A Service Health alert scoped to that resource group, which reports when Advisor finds a cost saving opportunity
An Advisor alert scoped to that resource group and the Cost category, with an action group that sends the email
A Resource Health alert on that resource group, which fires when Advisor marks one of its resources as wasteful

stem: An IT consultant hears news of a large outage affecting several Azure regions. The consultant has no access to any client subscription but wants to see whether Azure has published an incident. What should they check?

choices.text: The Azure status page, a public global view of Azure services across all regions that anyone can open
Azure Service Health, a personalized view of the services and regions used by a signed-in subscription
Azure Resource Health, which shows the current and past health of each resource in a subscription
Azure Advisor, which lists reliability recommendations for every Azure region affected by an outage

stem: Users report that one VM is unreachable. The admin wants to know whether Azure has detected a platform problem with that VM, such as an unexpected host reboot, or whether the cause is a user action like stopping it. Which tool should they use first?

choices.text: Application Insights for the VM, which records host reboots and stop operations for each VM in the subscription
Azure Resource Health for the VM, which shows its health status and whether a platform or a non-platform event caused it
Azure Advisor for the VM, which reports the VM's current health together with the reason it has stopped responding
The Azure status page, which lists every VM that is currently unavailable in each Azure region and the cause of each

stem: A team created Service Health alerts for all services and regions it uses. Last night one of its VMs became unavailable because of a hardware fault on its host, which Azure reported for that VM only, and no alert was sent. What should the team add?

choices.text: A Service Health alert with a different region selected, because the VM's region was not part of the alert
A Resource Health alert, because Service Health alerts do not fire for health events of individual resources
An Azure Advisor alert for the Reliability category, because Advisor reports hardware faults on the hosts
A Cost Management budget alert, because an unavailable VM stops billing and the cost drop signals a fault

stem: Right after a Windows VM is created, its CPU and disk charts appear in Azure Monitor with no setup. An admin also wants the VM's Windows event logs in a Log Analytics workspace, but none arrive. What is missing?

choices.text: A Service Health alert for the VM's region, because event collection starts only once a health alert exists
An Application Insights resource, because Windows event logs are collected only by application telemetry
A Resource Health check on the VM, because Resource Health copies the VM's event logs into the workspace
The Azure Monitor Agent installed in the VM, because data from inside the guest OS needs an agent

stem: A new operations team is learning how Azure Monitor stores data. Which TWO statements correctly describe Azure Monitor Metrics and Azure Monitor Logs? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Metrics are recorded only after an agent is installed on each resource, so new resources show no data until then
Logs can hold data only from Azure resources, so on-premises servers and other clouds need a separate monitoring tool
Logs are timestamped records with structured or free-form data, kept in a Log Analytics workspace and queried with KQL
Metrics are kept in a Log Analytics workspace and can be read only by writing KQL queries in the Log Analytics tool
Metrics are numeric values sampled at regular intervals and stored in a time-series database suited to fast alerting

stem: An engineer will write queries in Log Analytics and reuse them in log search alert rules and workbooks. Which query language should the engineer learn for this?

choices.text: Kusto Query Language (KQL), a read-only language for filtering and aggregating data in Azure Monitor Logs
Transact-SQL (T-SQL), the language of Azure SQL Database, which Log Analytics uses to query every log table
Bicep, the Azure deployment language, which Log Analytics uses to select and filter rows in each log table
PromQL, the Prometheus language, which Log Analytics uses for all log tables in a Log Analytics workspace

stem: An app writes the text "Payment gateway timeout" to its logs, which are collected into a Log Analytics workspace from 12 VMs. The team wants an alert when this message appears more than 5 times in 15 minutes across all VMs. Which alert type fits?

choices.text: A Service Health alert for the region of the VMs, because timeouts are reported as Azure service issues
An activity log alert on the VMs, because each logged message is written as an administrative operation
A log search alert rule that runs a KQL query on the workspace on a schedule and checks the count of matches
A metric alert rule on each VM's CPU percentage, because a high CPU value shows that the timeouts are happening

stem: An operations team is designing Azure Monitor action groups to use with several alert rules. Which TWO can an action group do when an alert fires? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Notify people by email, SMS, voice call or Azure mobile app push notification
Raise the alert rule's threshold automatically so that the same alert does not fire again
Decide which resources and signals the alert rule watches and the condition that fires it
Fix the cause of the alert by itself, for example by resizing the VM without any automation
Start automation such as a runbook, an Azure Function, a Logic Apps workflow or a webhook

stem: An online shop has almost no visitors between 1 a.m. and 6 a.m., so outages at night go unnoticed until morning. The team wants its public checkout URL tested every few minutes from several locations, with an alert if it fails. What should it use?

choices.text: A metric alert on the web app's request count, which fires when the number of user requests falls to zero
Azure Resource Health for the web app, which sends test requests to the public URL from several regions
Azure Advisor performance recommendations, which test the public URL at night and report response times
Application Insights standard availability tests, which send synthetic web requests from several locations

stem: On Monday morning an administrator finds that a production VM was deleted over the weekend. She needs to know who deleted it and exactly when. Where should she look first?

choices.text: Application Insights, which records every operation that users perform on the virtual machines in the subscription
The Azure activity log, which records each create, update and delete operation along with the identity that started it
Azure Advisor, which lists each deleted resource as a reliability recommendation together with the person who deleted it
Azure Resource Health, which keeps the VM's health history and reports the user who changed its status to Unavailable
